title: Source Availability and Reproduction
paragraphs: Appendix I Source Availability and Reproduction The available archive contains thesis sources, embedded chart coordinates, and a demonstration-telemetry JSON summary. It does not include the platform source tree, historical numerical engine, original R exports, respondent matrices, transcripts, posterior draws, or trip statements mentioned in the inherited research account. No source inspection, native software test, respondent-level reanalysis, or live platform experiment is certied by this version. Earlier implementation descriptions are historical reports requiring verication against a restored, versioned archive. I.1 What Can Be Reproduced Now The supplied workow can compile the document, regenerate diagrams from shared specications, inventory references and missing assets, hash available inputs, and produce a reviewer package. These are document and arithmetic checks, not replications of the eld study. Generated synthetic xtures used to check software are not participant records and never enter thesis results. 298

APPENDIX I. SOURCE AVAILABILITY AND REPRODUCTION 299 I.2 What Requires Additional Material Field reproduction needs original questionnaire responses, the instrument and scoring version, retained identiers, exclusion rationale, and analysis scripts. Qualitative reproduction needs original records, their verbatim, translated, or reconstructed status, the codebook, coding decisions, and consent-compatible access. Trip statements document trips, not participant identity, informed consent, or attentive listening. Historical simulation reproduction needs code, conguration, random-state denitions, calibration particles, all run logs, and outputs; Bayesian reproduction also needs priors, sampling settings, diagnostics, and posterior draws. I.3 Implementation and Measurement Boundaries A route name, test function, screenshot, or container specication does not establish successful treatment delivery. Before the prospective experiment, verify each active feature against its versioned implementation and reconcile acknowledged actions with archived events and committed state. Isolate condition-specic accounts, databases, media state, and message streams. Keep eld responses, synthetic accounts, and demonstration telemetry separate. Theoretical BRS components, a platform feedback posterior, and the 11-item questionnaire are dierent objects. Agreement among their names cannot establish equivalent scoring or validated uncertainty. The historical replication-percentile intervals and equal-tailed Bayesian intervals likewise retain distinct interpretations (Section 5.17).

APPENDIX I. SOURCE AVAILABILITY AND REPRODUCTION 301 I.4.1 Reserved Agent Hallucination and Divergence Diagnostics To separate platform eects from model artifacts, the extension will audit agent outputs along the three dimensions dened in Section 5.10: the evidence fabrication index (EFI), the platform state divergence (PSD), and the persona drift score (PDS) (Section 5.10.12, Equations 5.185.20). No executed values are reported below: the extension has not run, and the columns record the planned reporting structure, not measured quantities. A detector self-check must rst ag injected fabrications on a held-out benchmark whose factual state the pipeline knows, after which genuine logs ll the cells. The Pending markers are therefore not zero values or implied failure; they denote reserved evidence.
